extra.message: The session signing secret defaults to the hardcoded value 'dev-only-change-me'. If the SESSION_SECRET environment variable is not set, this known secret is used to sign all session tokens with URLSafeSerializer, allowing an attacker to forge valid session tokens for any user and bypass authentication.

The default database_url contains hardcoded credentials 'postgres:postgres' for the PostgreSQL connection. If the DATABASE_URL environment variable is not overridden, these credentials are used in production.
The session cookie is set with secure=False, meaning it will be transmitted over unencrypted HTTP connections. This allows network attackers to intercept session tokens via man-in-the-middle attacks.

The session cookie is set with secure=False on login, meaning it will be transmitted over unencrypted HTTP connections. This allows network attackers to intercept session tokens via man-in-the-middle attacks.

The password reset endpoint returns the reset_token in the API response body. Any caller can request a password reset for any email and immediately obtain the token, enabling full account takeover. Additionally, the conditional inclusion of the token (None when user not found) leaks whether an email is registered.

extra.message: The CSV import endpoint reads the entire uploaded file into memory with file.file.read() without any size limit. An attacker with admin/support_specialist role could upload a very large file to exhaust server memory, causing denial of service.
Hardcoded password 'Password123!' is used for all seeded demo users (admin, underwriter, support, borrower). If seed data persists in production, these known credentials allow full system access.

User-controlled 'host' parameter is directly concatenated into an OS command string passed to os.system(): 'ping -c 1 ' + host. An attacker can inject arbitrary shell commands using semicolons or backticks, achieving remote code execution on the server.

User-controlled 'fragment' parameter is directly concatenated into a Jinja2 Template string: Template('Result: ' + fragment).render(). This allows Server-Side Template Injection (SSTI), enabling arbitrary Python code execution via Jinja2 template syntax such as __import__('os').popen('...').

XML parser is configured with load_dtd=True, resolve_entities=True, and no_network=False, enabling processing of external entities with network access. User-supplied XML is parsed with this insecure configuration, allowing XXE attacks to read arbitrary files, perform SSRF, or cause DoS.

extra.message: User-controlled 'url' parameter is passed directly to urllib.request.urlopen() without validation or restriction. This allows Server-Side Request Forgery (SSRF), enabling an attacker to make the server send requests to arbitrary internal or external URLs, potentially accessing internal services, cloud metadata endpoints, or other restricted resources.

User-controlled 'packet_ref' parameter is used to construct a file path with BASE_EXPORT_DIR / packet_ref. Path traversal sequences like '../../etc/passwd' allow reading arbitrary files on the filesystem, since the path is not sanitized or validated before being passed to read_text().

extra.message: User-controlled 'card' parameter is rendered through a Jinja2 template using the |safe filter, which disables HTML auto-escaping. The result is returned as HTMLResponse, enabling cross-site scripting (XSS) since arbitrary HTML/JavaScript in the 'card' parameter will be rendered unescaped in the browser.

User-controlled 'lane' parameter is passed directly to RedirectResponse() without validation. An attacker can craft a URL with lane=https://evil.com to redirect users to an attacker-controlled site, enabling phishing attacks.

extra.message: User-controlled JSON payload is applied directly to the workset dictionary via workset.update(payload), allowing the attacker to overwrite security-sensitive fields like 'role', 'tier', 'approved', and 'balance', bypassing business logic constraints.

The request's Origin header is reflected directly into the Access-Control-Allow-Origin response header, with Access-Control-Allow-Credentials set to true. This allows any origin to make credentialed cross-origin requests to this endpoint, effectively bypassing the same-origin policy.

extra.message: The authorization decision for elevated access is based on the 'ops_badge' cookie or 'x-ops-badge' header, both of which are user-controlled. An attacker can set the cookie to 'lead' or the header to 'lead' to gain elevated privileges (elevated lane, full payroll, open casework), bypassing proper authentication/authorization.
